<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/index.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/work/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**74** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d707686ee33648063fc5a87b20b7e6376940d9c`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/index.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/work/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sharingModel (symbol, 49 pages)`, `created_at (literal, 49 pages)`, `current_user (literal, 45 pages)`, `owner_id (literal, 45 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **188** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d707686ee33648063fc5a87b20b7e6376940d9c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5ca028e3413e3533f0eec23389006fdd6b220896` — the merge of head `ef4fd2f76ee26ad8b8b09ba0fea38a6812db5917` into base `9d707686ee33648063fc5a87b20b7e6376940d9c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5ca028e3413e3533f0eec23389006fdd6b220896 && git checkout 5ca028e3413e3533f0eec23389006fdd6b220896
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9d707686ee33648063fc5a87b20b7e6376940d9c ef4fd2f76ee26ad8b8b09ba0fea38a6812db5917 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9d707686ee33648063fc5a87b20b7e6376940d9c && git merge --no-ff ef4fd2f76ee26ad8b8b09ba0fea38a6812db5917

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9d707686ee33648063fc5a87b20b7e6376940d9c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9d707686ee33648063fc5a87b20b7e6376940d9c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7db13dc8a1d49df6392b490449efb66724c59c86`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/work/sharing-rules.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/work/sys-task.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/work/sys-note.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/work/hooks.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/task-note-objects-36942.test.ts
Security-touching: yes

Full record on PR #36965 (card #36942), net diff against merge base `8e4ac50d430` (32 files, +2100 −5). Read: the card body and its nine comments (triage, claim 7128821530, the four os-dev reports and the final one 7139458322, seat decisions 7130212059, ruling record 7131539862), the PR body, the diff, and the cited code in the tree at this head. Check-runs on this head: 73 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`; the required contexts (Test Core and its ten shards, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate) are `success`, as are Check Changeset and Spec property liveness; Lint UI is `skipped`. The head has not moved since they completed.

The rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` and is not judged here: the ten locale bundles and three source-hash files under `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/`, `bundle-ownership.test.ts`, `scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts`, `work/work-objects.test.ts`, `work/index.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.declared-rule-mirrors.integration.test.ts`, `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` and the changeset's prose (its level and declaration lines are judged in ②).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `sys_note` and `sys_task` — right.** Both sit in sorted position (`sys_migration_journal` · `sys_note` · `sys_notification`; `sys_sso_provider` · `sys_task` · `sys_team`). The group is "the exact set that package registers", and `PlatformObjectsPlugin.init()` registers both at this head. The paired artifacts moved with it: the tenancy census (110 registered, 59 in reach, both `organization_id`), the ADR-0131 D10 inventory, the bundle-ownership list; the spec conformance test and `check:generated` are green on the head with no further spec diff, so `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` hold no enumerated copy. `packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts` is a hand-kept subset and may omit them.
- **Who reads the list, and whether membership is a behavioural switch.** Five readers do more than resolve a reference, each read at this head:
  - `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` (the action cross-reference, `isPlatformProvidedObjectName(action.objectName)`): a top-level action naming `sys_task` or `sys_note` was refused by `defineStack` on the base and is accepted now. This is an accept-set widening of a published door. Right as behaviour; the declaration is wrong, see ②.
  - `packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts` and its siblings: a reference to either name stops drawing the unknown-platform-name advisory. Right; pinned by the new item-6 case.
  - `packages/objectql/src/engine-lifecycle-health.ts` `resolvePrimaryDatasource`: every registered member votes for the primary datasource. The work manifest carries `scope: 'system'` and no `defaultDatasource` or `namespace`, exactly as the first platform-objects manifest, so both new names vote where `sys_migration` and `sys_unit` already vote; no new `system-objects-split`. Right.
  - `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`: a 404 on a registered platform name degrades to an empty result and is memoised. On a backend that does not carry the two objects the Console now shows an empty list for them instead of the load failure. That is the documented meaning of the registry there ("this deployment does not install the feature"). Right.
  - `packages/objectql/src/integrity/dangling-reference-audit.ts` reads the `plugin-security` group only. Untouched.
  The prefix readers (`hasPlatformObjectPrefix`: no recycle bin, the MCP `sys_` guard, the create-side read-only strip exemption, the user-deactivation assigned-work census) follow the name, not the list, and the object files and `hooks.ts` say so correctly.
- **`member_default` gains two object lines — right against the ruling.** `{ allowRead: true, allowCreate: true, allowEdit: true, allowDelete: false }` on each, the `sys_comment` shape; explicit allows only; no delete bit (ADR-0090 D5); no `allowTransfer`, `viewAllRecords` or `modifyAllRecords`; no row policy added; no other shipped set names either object, so an external member resolves no such line. The runtime test pins the exact shape.
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/platform-objects` root gains `SysTask`, `SysNote`, `TASK_DONE_STATUS`, `SYS_TASK_ASSIGNEE_SHARING_RULE`, `WORK_OBJECT_SHARING_RULES`, `installWorkObjectHooks`, `stampTaskCompletion`, `stampNoteHeading`, `firstLineOf`; the `./plugin` entry gains `WORK_OBJECTS_MANIFEST`; the published language packs gain the two objects' keys in eleven locales. All additions, none a removal.
- **ADR-0131 D10 fate — right.** Both rows are `attribution`, census `platform-census-main`, `anchors: []`, the `sys_unit` row's shape and citation. Members write the rows and the organization column is stamped from the writing context; step one links neither to a parent, so there is no anchor to name; under `single` a NULL row takes the Default Organization, otherwise it is reported. The inventory unit test and the three ceremony files are green in Test Core.
- **Declared sharing rule `sys_task_assignee` — right.** `type: 'criteria'`, `condition: 'record.assignee_id != null'`, `sharedWith: { type: 'field', value: 'assignee_id' }`, `accessLevel: 'edit'`, registered on the work manifest. `assignee_id` is `Field.user`, which the rule service's `fieldRecipientColumnIsUsable` accepts as a column that holds users; the per-record expansion (`recipientsNamedOnRecord`, `desiredGrantsForRule`) is the existing `field` path, and an empty assignee shares with nobody. The condition is not a match-all in form. Edit access for the assignee is what the ruling names.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/36942-platform-task-note-objects.md`: `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch. Both are in the fixed group. Patch is the level `Metadata-protocol: none` takes, and nothing here is breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed.

S3 (should-fix) — `Clause-②: no` is wrong on the PR body, the changeset and claim 7128821530; the line reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The criterion is whether the card widens a published accept set or enlarges a public surface, and this diff does both: `defineStack` now accepts a top-level action whose `objectName` is `sys_task` or `sys_note` (`stack.zod.ts`, the `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` arm; refused on the base), and the public surface grows as listed in ①. Both precedents for a roster addition declare the widening: #35488 (`sys_unit`, the same four-package shape) and changeset b5eb61d (`sys_lifecycle_state`). The path face already brought this review to tier, so no review was skipped; the declaration is still the audited line and must be true.

S4 (should-fix) — the changeset body ends "Members reach both through a permission set that grants the objects: the platform's member baseline grants neither." At this head `member_default` grants both read, create and edit. The sentence predates ruling 7131539862 and ships in `CHANGELOG.md` saying the opposite of the baseline. The frontmatter also omits `@objectstack/plugin-security` (the baseline grant) and `@objectstack/cli` (the two inventory rows), both of which this diff moves; #35488 names all four and gives each its own bullet. Replace the sentence with the grant as ruled (read, create, edit, no delete; rows stay with each object's private sharing) and add the two packages at patch.

- nit N1 — `Metadata-protocol: none`. The two precedents disagree: #35488 declared `none` at patch, b5eb61d declared `added` at minor for the same kind of roster addition. `none` is accepted here on the nearer precedent (no key, no metadata type, no schema value changes; a reference that already parsed now resolves). The fix round for S3 should say in one clause which reading it takes, since the action arm above is an accepted value by the letter of the rule.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question 1, three times (file surface: the spec roster, the i18n extract config, the runtime test, the census; then the inventory; then the declared-rule-mirrors test): seat decision A each time, claim amended. Answered. Each added path is a direct consequence of two new platform objects and one declared rule.
- Dev open question 2 (member baseline): ruled A by the maintainer, record 7131539862, with the rider and the falsifiable premise. Implemented as ruled in shape; the rider's measurement is S2 below.
- Dev open question 3 (navigation needs `requiresObject`): seat decision A, the contract stays; #36944 carries it. Answered, and the item-6 pin asserts both `defineStack` and the lint rule on the gated shape.
- Out-of-scope finding, the boot-time rule-hook gap: filed #36982, fixed by #37012, merged into this head; the runtime test now runs on one boot with the organization inserted after `bootstrap()`. Answered.
- Out-of-scope notes with no carrier: both objects are absent from the app-facing platform catalog; as `sys_` names they get no recycle bin, are not AI-readable without `aiReadable`, and are skipped by the user-deactivation assigned-work census. The last one matters for a task object (a deactivated user's assigned tasks are not surfaced) and is a follow-up card for the seat to file under #36941; it does not block this head.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The hooks act on the row being written; the sharing rule rides the existing rule service.
- Escalation: S1 goes to the maintainer through the seat, privately. Nothing about it is written here.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`.** Holds against the module's own maintenance contract ("adding an object to a platform package means adding its name here") and against its first consumer, the item-6 navigation pin in `@objectstack/lint`. Sorted position, the conformance test and the paired census are right (①). Attempt to break it: a host that declares its own `sys_task` is refused by the registry's single-owner rule and `PlatformObjectsPlugin` logs the refusal at `warn` instead of booting without the objects silently, while the roster still says the name is platform-provided; the lint answer and the runtime answer then differ only on a host that already fails registration loudly. Holds.

**`default-permission-sets.ts` against the ruling.** The two lines are the ruled shape, and the comment cites the ruling verbatim. One sentence of the comment does not hold against the test it cites, S2.

S2 (should-fix) — the comment says the assignee's edit lands because "the `owner_only_writes` floor below defers to an `edit` share, measured there too, so no per-object alternative is added", and the PR body and the test docblock say the same. The runtime test does not measure it. Its member context is `{ userId, tenantId, positions: [], permissions: [], org_user_ids }`, and `owner_only_writes` declares `positions: ['org_member']`; `RLSCompiler`'s applicability filter drops a policy whose domain the caller's held positions do not meet, and the middleware reads those positions from the context (`context?.positions ?? []`). So for all three test members the floor is outside its domain and never binds: the assignee's update is admitted without the floor being asked, and the rider's condition ("if the runtime test measures that `owner_only_writes` refuses an assignee's edit despite the edit share") was not put to the test. A real member's context carries `org_member` (`resolve-authz-context.ts`). Read from the code, the outcome is expected to be the same for a real member (the sharing service's positive verdict replaces the platform floor where it is the write class's last term, #5492), but that is a reading, not the measurement the ruling asks for. Fix: build the three members' contexts with the positions the auth layer gives a member, re-run, and either keep the sentence or add the rider's one per-object update alternative. The read half of the premise pin does not depend on positions (no position-scoped select policy applies to either object) and stands.

**The falsifiable-premise pin.** One boot after #37012, organization and members inserted after `bootstrap()`; the second member's `findOne` by id is `null` and the list omits the row, for the task and for the note; the assignee of another task reads no note; the second member's update answers `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` / 404 with the row unchanged. On the composition the test boots, the pin is the premise. nit N2 — the pin covers `find` and `findOne`; a count or aggregate as the second member, and the old assignee's read after a reassignment (the docblock's "the share moves when the assignee changes"), ride existing machinery and are not pinned for these objects.

**Attempt to break the permission posture** (could a member read or edit another member's task or note because of this diff). Read at this head, on the composition the runtime test boots and the stock served slate:
- REST data and list, and the cross-object search door: every one reaches the engine with the caller's context; `effectiveSharingModel` answers `private` for an explicit `private` on a `sys_` name, neither object is on the sharing bypass list, and search composes the same two layers. Closed.
- MCP data tools: `sys_` objects are refused unless the object opts in to AI read; neither declares it, and the write tools admit no `sys_` object at all. Closed.
- Ownership: the declared `owner_id` is governed by the owner-anchor step (it keys on the column being present, not on its provenance): an insert naming another owner and an update changing the owner both need the transfer grant, which the baseline does not carry, so an assignee with the edit share cannot take the record. Closed.
- Comments, activity and attachments on a task or note: each gate asks whether the caller can read the parent record. Closed.
- The create-side read-only strip skips `sys_` objects; `hooks.ts` assigns `completed_at` and `heading` over the writer's value on insert, as its docblock says, so a client cannot forge either. Holds.

S1 (should-fix) — security finding, routed privately.

**`sharing-rules.ts`, `sys-task.object.ts`, `sys-note.object.ts`, `hooks.ts`, `plugin.ts`.** Sentence by sentence against the code: the object docblocks' account of who sees a row matches the sharing service and the owner-anchor stamp; `hooks.ts` matches `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` (the `sys_` exemption) and the update-side strip; `plugin.ts` registers the work manifest separately so a refusal is reported and the infrastructure manifests stay registered, and installs the hooks under the work package id. `stampNoteHeading` on a predicate update that writes only an empty title leaves the stored heading as it was; nit N3 — that row then keeps a stale heading until its next by-id write. No effect on access.

**`organization-ownership-inventory.ts`.** Right (①).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36942-platform-task-note-objects`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · L1 · head `7db13dc8a1d49df6392b490449efb66724c59c86` · 2026-11-24T17:49Z

Seat L1 over the whole PR, beside the contract review at this head (record ID: 7139727107). The code, tests and translations hold: card items 1–7 and the four acceptance tests are delivered (`Fixes #36942` is right); all 32 files sit inside the amended claim, each out-of-original-scope file required by a gate; seat decision A on the declared-rule mirrors test narrows the helper to the fixture's object with no assertion weakened; the runtime test now boots once after #37012 and keeps the ruling's premise pin; ten locales plus `en` carry the same 33 leaves; the census is regenerated by its generator; 73 check-runs, none failed.

M1 (must-fix) — the changeset's last sentence says the platform's member baseline "grants neither". At this head `member_default` grants `sys_task` and `sys_note` read, create and edit, no delete (ruling 7131539862, A). It ships as CHANGELOG text. Rewrite it to state the grant as ruled, rows staying with each object's private sharing. (Contract review S4.)
M2 (must-fix) — the changeset frontmatter omits two published packages this diff moves: `@objectstack/plugin-security` (the baseline grant ships in `dist`) and `@objectstack/cli` (the two `organization-ownership-inventory.ts` fate rows ship in `dist`). Add both at `patch`, each with its own sentence. (Contract review S4.)
S1 (should-fix) — `Clause-②: no` should be `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset: new root exports from `@objectstack/platform-objects`, two names in `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE`, and a baseline that now allows creates and edits it refused. Nothing narrows; the level stays `patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none` stands (no authorable value moves from refused to accepted; `defineStack` judges `sys_*` by prefix before and after). (Contract review S3.)
S2 (should-fix) — the runtime test's members carry `positions: []`, so `owner_only_writes` (bound to `positions: ['org_member']`) never applies there, and the PR's "assignee edit lands under the floor, measured" claim is unmeasured. Give the members the `org_member` position (or the binding the stock posture gives a member) and re-measure the assignee's edit and the stranger's refused edit under it. (Contract review S2.)
S3 (should-fix) — security, held for the maintainer: a security item from the contract review (its S1) is with the maintainer through a private channel; this PR does not land until he answers, and the answer may add a change to this PR. No detail here.

Seat follow-up filed: #37058 (skills `platform-catalog.md` lists neither object); the PR body names it before ACCEPT.
Nits: the `member_default` ablation was measured on the two-boot test (the creator's insert refusal does not depend on the boot count — accepted); count/aggregate and reassignment are not pinned; a predicate update writing only an empty title leaves the old note heading (documented in code).

Next: the dev folds M1, M2, S1, S2 in one push; S3 waits on the maintainer.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ef4fd2f76ee26ad8b8b09ba0fea38a6812db5917`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + .changeset/36942-platform-task-note-objects.md, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/task-note-objects-36942.test.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta record on PR #36965 (card #36942), from the reviewed head `7db13dc8a1d` to `ef4fd2f76ee`. Three commits: merge `719ef290776` of main, rework `ab1bfc643c0`, merge `ef4fd2f76ee` of main. Read: the rework diff `719ef290776..ab1bfc643c0`, both merges, the PR body at this head, card comments 7141061822 and 7142313159, and the cited code in the tree at this head. Nothing was built or run.

- **Both merges are clean.** `git merge-tree --write-tree` of each merge's two parents gives the merge's own tree: `be90c4e438e` for `719ef290776`, `bf18c39fe98` for `ef4fd2f76ee`. Neither merge carries a hand edit.
- **The merges move no file of this PR.** Main brought 110 and 112 files; none is among the PR's 32. The PR's net diff against its merge base `9d707686ee3` is 32 files, +2118 −5: the reviewed diff plus the rework's two files.
- **Check-runs on this head, read once:** 68 runs. Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset and Spec property liveness are `success`; Lint UI is `skipped`. Test Core shards 1, 3, 9 and 10 were still `in_progress`; the other six are `success`. The seat reads Test Core's roll-up before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The rework changes no accept set and no public surface.** It edits the changeset (two frontmatter lines, the `Clause-②` line, the closing paragraphs) and one constant in the runtime test (`MEMBER_POSITIONS`). No product file moves; every judgment of the prior record's ① stands as written.
- **The merges change nothing this PR's surface rests on.** Read on the main side, where a path could bear on it:
  - `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`, `default-permission-sets.ts`, the sharing service and the RLS compiler: not touched by either merge.
  - `packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts`: main reworks how a held reference is reported (a `reason`, owner transfer). It names neither object, and the prior record's note (a `sys_` object is outside that census) is main's behaviour, not this PR's.
  - `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`: a new cross-set advisory on fields that carry `requiredPermissions`. Neither object declares such a field.
  - `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`: comment lines only.
  - `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts`: a tool-name roster, a different list.
- **The roster hit is unchanged from the reviewed head.** `sys_note` and `sys_task` sit in `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` exactly as reviewed.
